reason: This passage recounts the story of Naaman's healing (2 Kings 5) and does not depict Hebrew people suffering greatly, nor does any leader blame them for suffering. The text centers on Naaman (a Syrian military commander) seeking healing from leprosy through the prophet Elisha. When the King of Israel initially reacts with distress to a diplomatic request, Elisha responds with reassurance and offers a path to healing—not blame. The narrative contains no element of leaders attributing suffering to fault or guilt of the Hebrew people.
